description: Magna International Inc. operates as an automotive supplier in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Body Exteriors & Structures, Power & Vis
description_full: Magna International Inc. operates as an automotive supplier in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Body Exteriors & Structures, Power & Vision, Seating Systems, and Complete Vehicles. The company offers design and vehicle concepts, complete vehicle engineering and integration, human-machine interface, developing modules and systems, platform solutions, prototyping and low-volume manufacturing, vehicle safety testing, aerospace, and integrating functionality, features, and ADAS; and complete vehicle solutions, body-in-white, paint, and assembly complete vehicle manufacturing products. It also provides engineering services for commercial vehicles, such as propulsion engineering, software and simulation, testing services, and smart production; OPTiForm, a battery enclosure, steel battery enclosures, aluminum battery enclosures, and hybrid battery enclosures; battery enclosure production and engineering solutions; SmartAccess, a B-Pillarless power door system; and composite EV battery covers. In addition, it offers energy management solutions; hot stamping, high strength steels, aluminum castings, and high-pressure vacuum casting; suspension links and arms, twist axle, carbon fiber subframe, and frames; ADAS and Automated Driving, including Cameras, thermal sensing, interior sensing, complete radar portfolio, and compute units; and chassis control, glow plug control, powertrain control, and mechatronic control modules. Further, it provides exterior and interior products comprising assist steps, engineered glass, exterior solutions, greenhouse surrounds, lighting, mechatronics, mirrors, and seating; and powertrain products consisting BEV, Hybrid, and ICE powertrain, as well as modules and components, and energy storage systems. Magna International Inc. was founded in 1957 and is based in Aurora, Canada.

financial_summary: Magna International, Inc. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $16.1B market cap on $42.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +3% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $2.3B in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.34× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.1× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.8×.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 5.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

E-commerce margin compression and tariff exposure — digital competition erodes pricing power while trade policy reshuffles supply-chain cost structures overnight.
Brand relevance decay — shifting consumer preferences and social-media-driven trends can strand inventory and invalidate positioning faster than product cycles can adapt.

sect: Its 3% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (8%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.38x its revenue share).
It accounts for 0.8% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-9.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 35% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 7% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 16% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 38% and a beta of 1.09, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.25 vs 5y 1.12), so read it loosely.
About $67.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 56% in the 2020 crash, 46% in the 2022 bear market and 75% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 61% below its DCF fair value of $159, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 27%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $118 to $218 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Cyclical peers: EV/EBITDA 5.4 vs 11.2 and P/FCF 7.0 vs 16.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 63% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 14.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 17 covering analysts target $72.00 on average, 16% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.8%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.45).
It converts 5% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 4.34x, but high accruals (-8.8% of assets).
ROE of 7% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.9% of revenue on R&D.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.1x net debt to EBITDA ($1.6B of cash against $4.7B of debt), with interest covered 4.8x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.5% over 3 years, 5.2% over 5 years and 2.7% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 6.9% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 1.4% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.8x, 3.1% of sales), a maintenance pace.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 23.2% on average.
own: Insiders own 5.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 77%.
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (0.9% in buybacks and 3.2% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 1.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 34 consecutive years, raising it 3.1% a year over the last five.
people: With about 156,000 employees, each generates about $269K of revenue, 0.7x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 2.7% a year.
That works out to $15K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $8.0M (30x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
